record_notes.DCP-LETT-1433: June 8 with supplied 1851 year. Requests Alder loan of Loven plate through Hancock for Sowerby copying; an earlier tracing and dissected Steenstrup specimen are distinct artifacts. Requests Ibla attachment on a smooth support, then recalls four purchased specimens on rugged supports and narrows the request. Bryozoa papers have recently been read, without an exact reading day. Deleted dissection request is reported in apparatus, not silently restored to sent prose. No surviving incoming cover identifies this initiated request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1437: June 22 with supplied 1851 year. Thanks for assistance with the book and Alder kindness; declines offered Ibla because supports are rugged and permits manuscript retention while asking not to lose pages. The offer follows June 8 but its actual incoming text is missing. Both 1433 and 1437 are Darwin outgoing, not a prompt pair. Manuscript identity remains editorially probable.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1495: December 25 with supplied 1852 year based on journal work on Verruca. Full five-part case moves from initial mechanical preference toward hypothetical chemical excavation: no detected apparatus, ligament restriction, attached central cement, protective epidermis/slate versus marble, and possible cement-duct acid. Acid secretion remains hypothesis. Requests Hancock judgment and noncalcareous support specimens; Alcippe examination still promised in two weeks, not completed, and manuscript return is queried. Prior Hancock observations and later cautionary reply are unlocated incoming texts. Later published outcomes remain apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1497: January 10 with supplied 1853 year and dated endorsement. Thanks for missing long cautionary reply, clarifies marginal versus central erosion, promises Bate enquiry, and distinguishes several slate specimens from hundreds on Laminaria. Full diagram viewed in P1, not extracted P2: cross-section labels ligament and a marks around the central hollow. Welcomes Owen, Dana and Hancock acceptance of complemental males, agrees on cross-fertilisation, critiques Steenstrup, and says Alcippe paper was read the other evening. Manuscript has now returned; damaged P3 lacunae remain. No authentic incoming caution letter survives here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1498: January 29 with supplied 1853 year. Alcippe anatomical study is now underway and generative system perplexing; asks dry shells across seasons and possible fishermen collections. Apologises for cutting up all lent specimens, a contemporary belief later qualified by August 1854 surviving specimens. Final assertion that Alcippe has no relation to South American burrower is current interpretation, not final modern taxonomy. Surmises explicitly may be blunders. No surviving prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1500: February 10 with supplied 1853 year. Finds males on previously imperfectly examined material and no longer urgently needs specimens, though requests future dry distribution and cavity specimens. Explains initial failure to recognise a male and difficulty of anatomy. This is a same-author follow-up to January 29, not an incoming prompt reply. Later book statement about discarded Bryozoa and final family choice is apparatus, not an already completed decision here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1501: February 12 with supplied 1853 year. Full thirteen-block anatomical account, from mouth/cirri and absent anus through female organs, rudimentary penis, larval metamorphosis and males, excavation and unresolved classification. Positive wording is expressly for brevity. Two diagrams independently viewed at extracted P10 and P11, not P11/P12: male positions marked on female outline, and inclined larval position above a surface with dotted lower outline. Raw HTML has literal 125 with superscript th and no fraction markup; reliable length rendering is held rather than treating this as 125 inches or silently reconstructing 1/25. P11 mechanical excavation claim concerns Alcippe, not a reversal of Verruca chemical hypothesis. Classification remains undecided. No surviving prompt, but Hancock 1505 explicitly replies to this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1504: February 25 with supplied 1853 year. Two questions ask Alcippe depth and collection date of spirit specimens; separately notes recently posted dry specimens were shrivelled despite abundant males. Does not answer same-day Hancock draft 1505, which itself explicitly answers February 12. Later book depth of 15–20 fathoms is not an answer present in this letter. March 30 acknowledges a missing answer note, whose wording is not supplied by the current outgoing questions.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1505: February 25, 1853 autograph draft. Explicitly acknowledges long February 12 letter and answers cushion homology, parasitic males and classification. Explains weight given to cirri/alimentary relationships and why Alcippe may not fit sessile or pedunculate groups, with admitted imperfect knowledge. Specimen collection by coastal gentlemen and Cullercoats visits is prospective. March 30 former classification note strongly identifies the corresponding communication as received; exact dispatch/receipt and final sent wording are not established by draft alone. Cannot answer same-day 1504 questions, which are absent here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1509: March 30 with supplied 1853 year. P1 distinguishes a note received this morning answering queries from a former note received some time since with Alcippe classification remarks. Former note corresponds to 1505; fresh answer note is missing, not 1504 (Darwin outgoing). P3–6 gives changed comparative classification difficulty after completing South American burrower and a hypothesis about trituration from Alcippe cushions and analogous oesophageal teeth. P1 mixed-input acknowledgement and P2 inventory reminder are outside accepted response scope. Draft correspondence received by this date, exact earlier receipt unknown; modern common-order classification remains later editorial knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1580: August 24 with supplied 1854 year. Now one or two undissected spirit specimens remain despite January 1853 statement all were cut; asks return or museum donation, reports Bate Plymouth find, and separates Madeira material from Davis Strait specimen definitely to return. Oxynaspis specimens already taken for museums, without inferring shipment completion. Volume printed but publication only expected soon. Hancock permission and any recent return instructions are unlocated; older outgoing letters are context, not incoming prompts.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1316: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. Sunday March 31 OR April 7, 1850, inferred through Oxynaspis request and 1321 receipt; dating chain is interdependent and no independent exact-day witness here. Hancock now evidently has manuscript and damaged mollusc shipment; Darwin permits long retention. Identifies B. cranchii, asks Greenland Balanus with permission for disarticulation, and asks Madeira specimen because own are decayed. Explicitly changes Machairis to Oxynaspis here, not at original October mention. Missing Hancock letter supplies damage/range information; no actual completion of new requested examination.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1321: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. Day 15 with supplied April 1850, editorially linked to 1316 request. New specimens safely arrived by this delayed acknowledgment; Madeira one deliberately held until return to Pedunculata work, not already dissected. Balanus identified with little/no opening, return promised, earlier mixed specimens recalled. Greenland latitude requested, Iceland occurrence already known. Still convinced all Lithotrya bore but mechanism uncertain. Later Balanus priority name in apparatus does not replace current names. No exact specimen arrival day or surviving incoming cover.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1327: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. May 12 with supplied 1850 year. Explicitly only just read Hancock 1848 mollusc-boring paper because periodicals not read promptly; publication and ownership do not establish earlier knowledge. Sends one of three Lithotrya specimens after moult, distinguishes moulting scales from valves; lacks basal cup specimen though previously borrowed examples. Remains undecided between entering and enlarging existing hole or initial larval boring; planned Clisia examination future. Missing Hancock request for more information/specimens is reported, not preserved. Published 1851/1854 conclusions remain later.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1378: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. December 25 with supplied 1850 year. Cup/discs do not themselves move; explanation revises earlier model, not complete hindsight knowledge. Cement gland/ovary interpretation is contemporary claim, not modern verified biology. Fractions are 1/20 or 1/16 inch, confirmed raw MathML. Literal [SYMBOL HERE] does not preserve the enclosed plate; zero image nodes. It accompanies P1 distinction between marginal erosion and central hollow. No scale or newly inferred chemical mechanism is supplied by the drawing.

Viewed schematic female outline with Mouth and orifice into sack labels and a Males label pointing toward a cross at one side; another cross lies on the other side. It illustrates P10 male attachment positions, not the anatomy of the reduced male itself.

Viewed unlabelled sketch of an inclined small body above a horizontal surface, with a dotted outline below the surface. Read with P11 proposed initial position and burrow; angle, scale and depth are not quantitatively specified.
